quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They work as well as a face shield.
They work as well as goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from wind.
They protect you from objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat and roll off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to catch up to the group. More experienced riders can also watch them from behind.

questions.question: Is wearing a riding jacket a good idea in hot weather?

options.text: Yes, it can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, plus other safety benefits.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader at the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead.

questions.question: What gear should you be in when stopped?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen the most?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be seen better. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in snow, rain, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward while braking, your front wheel gets more traction. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when roads are slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. If you can see through the vehicle, you don't need extra distance.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance behind the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are five times more likely to get a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: The center part of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars often collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars often collect.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of the lane. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found there.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds of distance. You may need extra time to notice the vehicle in front has stopped and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When a vehicle tries to pass you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center part of the lane.
Move to the left part of the lane.
Move to the right part of the lane.
Not worry about which part of the lane you are in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center part of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center part of your lane. This keeps you farther from the passing vehicle and reduces collision risk.

questions.question: Of crashes between a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the driver not yielding the right-of-way to the motorcycle?
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left part of your lane.
Ride in the center part of your lane.
Ride in the right part of your lane.
Try to move onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side nearest the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to turn.
Do not drag your feet on the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet—you could lose control. Always watch for other traffic on the road.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they do not get caught on anything.

questions.question: Who sets the pace when a group of riders travels together?
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders are left behind.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks on a surface with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You will still be able to steer your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles use a staggered formation. Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Riders on three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.
